About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For
our future fab in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and
committed: Chemical Quality & Laboratory Engineer (m/f/d) Are you
ready to design, build, and run a state-of-the-art analytical
chemistry laboratory from the ground up? As a Chemical Quality &
Laboratory Engineer (m/f/d) at ESMC, you will be key to establishing
our chemical laboratory infrastructure in Dresden. Starting on January 2027, you will manage our analytical instruments, set up
testing standards, and verify the quality of incoming materials and
facility chemical systems. Collaborating closely with our advanced
teams in Taiwan and leading a small group of local technicians, you
will directly safeguard the production quality of Europe's newest
premier semiconductor fab! Tasks Lab Infrastructure Setup: Design,
establish, and optimize our on-site chemical lab capacity, process
setups, and analytical capabilities. Instrument Management: Lead the
operation, calibration, and maintenance of high-precision analytical
equipment, with a focus on ICP-MS, GC-MS, PTR-MS, and Ion
Chromatography (IC). Material Quality Control: Execute routine and
event-triggered monitoring of incoming chemicals and raw materials to
ensure strict compliance with manufacturing standards. Technical
Writing: Define Operational Instructions (OIs) and Standard Operating
Procedures (SOPs) for the laboratory environment. Team Leadership:
Supervise, train, and coordinate a small, dedicated group of
laboratory technicians. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with
fab and facility teams to troubleshoot chemical events, support
continuous improvement projects (CIP), and verify tool certifications.
Emergency On-Duty Support: Participate in weekend and night-shift
on-duty rotations to handle urgent chemical safety or quality
escalations. Profile Must-Have: Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s
degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Material Science, or a
related scientific discipline. Technical Experience: 0 to 3 years of
hands-on experience in chemical analysis, with deep knowledge of
analytical techniques such as ICP-MS, GC-MS, PTR-MS, or Ion
Chromatography (IC). Analytical Skillset: Experience in standard
sample preparation, calibration curves, statistical process control
(SPC) data interpretation, and analytical instrument troubleshooting.
Soft Skills: Strong collaborative mindset, intercultural openness,
resilience under pressure, and a structured, detail-oriented approach
to safety and quality. Languages: Fluency in English (written and
spoken) is required. Nice-to-Have: Prior experience in a semiconductor
manufacturing environment or cleanroom chemical lab management.
Knowledge of European chemical regulations (such as REACH) and safety
standards. Basic programming skills (e.g., Python, R, or SQL) for
analytical data processing. Basic communication skills in German
and/or Mandarin. We offer Security & Perspective: A permanent
employment contract and career advancement opportunities in one of
Europe's leading semiconductors fabs. Company Pension Plan & Financial
Benefits: We support your financial well-being with our robust company
pension plan. As an ESMC employee, you also benefit directly from
TSMC’s performance through an exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan
(ESPP). Training & Development: At the TSMC Newcomer Training Center,
gain a deeper understanding of the processes involved in operating
complex semiconductor equipment through unique hands-on training,
while you continuously expand your knowledge. Health & Well-Being: An
annual budget for your health and well-being (e.g., for sports
classes, massages, or relaxation) helps you stay fit. Meals &
Transportation: Enjoy a daily meal allowance as well as a subsidized
public transportation (e.g., for the Deutschlandticket). Additional
contact details Please apply with your english resume.

About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For
our future fab in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and
committed: Supplier Quality Engineer – Semiconductor Materials
(m/f/d) Starting on January 27, you can become a key safeguard for
Europe’s newest, most advanced semiconductor manufacturing process.
As a Supplier Quality Engineer – Semiconductor Materials (m/f/d) at
ESMC, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality and reliability
of all incoming materials and services used in our Dresden fabrication
facility. By collaborating with global suppliers and our internal
engineering, procurement, and laboratory teams, you will establish a
stable quality baseline that matches our mother fabs in Taiwan. This
role is an exciting opportunity to combine your technical knowledge of
material science with supplier management and big data analytics to
protect our production from material excursions! Tasks Incoming
Quality Assurance: Establish and maintain a stable statistical
baseline for incoming materials and services to ensure local wafer
quality aligns with our international mother fabs. Supplier Quality
Management: Conduct comprehensive supplier quality system assessments,
onsite audits, risk management, and process change control (PCN)
reviews. Excursion Prevention: Utilize statistical process control
(SPC) data and key performance indicators (KPIs) to proactively
monitor supplier performance and prevent material deviations.
Collaborative Problem Solving: Lead cross-functional troubleshooting
teams alongside suppliers and internal laboratory, facility, and
procurement departments to quickly resolve quality issues.
Cross-Border Alignment: Align requirements and share Best Known
Methods (BKMs) across different time zones, communicating effectively
with internal management and executive supplier representatives.
Continuous Improvement: Build trust-based, professional relationships
with suppliers to encourage proactive transparency and continuous
quality improvements. Profile Must-Have: Education: Bachelor’s or
Master’s degree in Material Science, Material Engineering,
Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Physics, or a closely related
technical field. Experience: 0 to 3 years of professional experience,
ideally in the semiconductor industry or related high-tech sectors
(e.g., photovoltaics, chemicals, pharmaceuticals). Core Technical
Skills: Familiarity with basic material quality management,
statistical data analysis, or process change control. Interpersonal &
Communication Skills: High intercultural open-mindedness, strong
initiative, and the confidence to communicate effectively with
international teams and senior management. Languages: Fluent in
English (written and spoken) is required. Nice-to-Have: Practical
experience in semiconductor fabrication operations, process
engineering, or physical/chemical laboratory analysis. Familiarity
with structured problem-solving methods (e.g., 8D, 5 Whys) and
supplier auditing. Basic conversational skills in German and/or
Mandarin. We offer Security & Perspective: A permanent employment
contract and career advancement opportunities in one of Europe's
leading semiconductors fabs. Company Pension Plan & Financial
Benefits: We support your financial well-being with our robust company
pension plan. As an ESMC employee, you also benefit directly from
TSMC’s performance through an exclusive Employee Stock Purchase Plan
(ESPP). Relocation Support for Dresden: Moving for us? We’ll provide
you with all the support you will need for your relocation and your
start in Dresden. Training & Development: At the TSMC Newcomer
Training Center, gain a deeper understanding of the processes involved
in operating complex semiconductor equipment through unique hands-on
training, while you continuously expand your knowledge. Health &
Well-Being: An annual budget for your health and well-being (e.g., for
sports classes, massages, or relaxation) helps you stay fit. Meals &
Transportation: Enjoy a daily meal allowance as well as a subsidized
public transportation (e.g., for the Deutschlandticket). Additional
contact details Please apply with your english resume.

About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For
our future fab in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and
committed: SPC & Metrology Quality Engineer (m/f/d) Are you passionate
about turning complex production data into robust manufacturing
stability? As an SPC & Metrology Quality Engineer (m/f/d) at ESMC, you
will be at the heart of our quality defense team in Dresden. Starting on January 2027, you will take ownership of the quality, calibration,
and tool matching of inline metrology systems (such as OCD, CDSEM, and
Overlay). Simultaneously, you will drive our Statistical Process
Control (SPC) system enhancements to predict manufacturing risks,
analyze data trends, and prevent process deviations. This role is a
unique opportunity to combine physical engineering with advanced
statistical analysis in a brand-new, state-of-the-art semiconductor
fab. Tasks Metrology Quality Assurance: Oversee the performance and
accuracy of critical inline metrology tools (including CDSEM, OCD, and
Overlay) to ensure stable process measurement. Tool Performance
Matching: Develop, implement, and monitor calibration and cross-fab
matching methods to guarantee uniform measurements across all
metrology tools. SPC System Enhancement: Drive the continuous
improvement of SPC systems, including control limit setup, CPK
monitoring, process audits, and data analysis. Statistical Analysis &
Risk Prevention: Apply advanced statistical methods (such as Design of
Experiments (DOE), sampling plans, and reliability modeling) to
predict risks and resolve quality issues. Data-Driven Development:
Program and develop custom statistical algorithms and analysis scripts
to automate quality monitoring and defense reporting. HQ
Collaboration: Partner with engineering teams at our Taiwan
headquarters to align local metrology and SPC standards with global
best practices. Profile Must-Have: Education: Bachelor’s or
Master’s degree in Material Engineering, Statistics, Industrial
Engineering, Physics, or a closely related technical field.
Professional Background: 0 to 3 years of experience in high-tech
manufacturing, ideally within the semiconductor industry. Statistical
Foundation: Strong knowledge of Statistical Process Control (SPC)
procedures, CPK analysis, and statistical evaluation techniques.
Programming Skills: Proficiency in statistical software/programming
languages such as JMP or R. Languages: Fluent in English (written and
spoken) for everyday communication in our international company.
Onboarding: Readiness to participate in an extended, hands-on training
assignment in Taiwan. Nice-to-Have: Hands-on experience with metrology
tools (CDSEM, OCD, or Overlay inspection systems). Programming skills
in Python. A certified Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt. Basic
conversational skills in German and/or Mandarin. We offer Help build a
completely new semiconductor manufacturing site in Europe. Work in a
highly international environment with colleagues across Europe, Taiwan
and the US. Shape processes instead of maintaining existing
structures. Participate in global projects and cross-functional
collaboration. International onboarding including 9-12 months of
training in Taiwan. Additional contact details Please apply with your
english resume.

Thinking of doing your PhD in the Life Sciences? The International PhD Programme (IPP) Mainz is offering talented scientists the chance to work on cutting edge research projects. As an IPP PhD student, you will join a community of exceptional scientists working on diverse topics ranging from how organisms age or how our DNA is repaired, to how epigenetics regulates cellular identity or neural memory. The research group of Anton Khmelinskii in collaboration with Jan Padeken offers the following PhD project:
The progressive deterioration of protein homeostasis (proteostasis) is a primary hallmark of aging. As organisms age, the functionality of the proteostasis network, comprised of molecular chaperones, the ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy, declines, leading to the accumulation of misfolded and aggregated proteins that compromise cellular viability. Proteostatic decline is not merely a consequence of aging but an early, causal event whereby loss of proteostasis precedes and predicts organismal decline, and its onset is sufficient to accelerate aging. Conversely, genetic or pharmacological enhancement of proteostasis network capacity can extend lifespan and suppresses age-related disease associated with protein misfolding across multiple model systems. These observations raise fundamental questions: what endogenous small molecules sustain proteostasis during aging, can their supplementation prevent neurodegenerative (and other protein folding diseases) and slow the aging process?

PhD project: Therapeutic applications of small molecule modulators of proteostasis

Organisms across all domains of life employ the accumulation of small organic osmolytes, which include molecules such as betaine and taurine, to mitigate proteotoxic stress. Recent work has also demonstrated anti-aging properties of this molecules, through yet unclear mechanisms. This project aims at dissecting the mode of action of different osmolytes using human cellular model systems and C. elegans as a model of organismal aging. We would like to address the following questions:

1. How do osmolytes affect cellular and organismal physiology?
2. Which types of stresses can be mitigated with exogenous osmolytes?
3. What types of protein misfolding pathologies (e.g., neurodegenerative diseases including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Alzheimers's, Parkinson's, Huntington's) can be ameliorated with exogenous osmolytes?

The project is part of an ongoing collaboration between the Khmelinskii and Padeken groups, which gives you the opportunity to become an expert in a wide range of methods and experimental approaches. This includes transcriptomics, proteomics, cell and molecular biology, fluorescence microscopy and advanced high-throughput mutagenesis screening.

If you are interested in this project, please select Khmelinskii/Padeken as your group preference in the IPP application platform. Are you an ambitious scientist looking to push the boundaries of research while interacting with colleagues from multiple disciplines and cultures? Then joining the IPP is your opportunity to give your scientific career a flying start!
All you need is:

Master or equivalent
Interactive personality & good command of English
2 letters of reference

Exciting, interdisciplinary projects in a lively international environment, with English as our working language

Advanced training in scientific techniques and professional skills
Access to our state-of-the-art Core Facilities and their technical expertise

Fully funded positions with financing until the completion of your thesis
A lively community ofmore than 200 PhD students from 44 different countries

For more details on the projects offered and how to apply via the online form using the apply button.

jobs.occupation: Research associates (m/f/x) in scientific computing (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.8725 hours/week = 75%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Research associates (m/f/x) in scientific computing

The chair of numerical mathematics at the Ruhr University Bochum focuses on the development of efficient algorithms for solving problems in the natural and engineering sciences. A special emphasis is on hyperbolic conservation laws and high‑dimensional problems. We develop efficient numerical methods exploiting low‑rank tensor techniques and mixed‑precision algorithms. Moreover, we are interested in structure‑preserving numerical methods that are particularly adapted to the physical structure of the modeling equations, as well as in hybrid methods that couple models of different complexity for optimal efficiency. We are participating in the Collaborative Research Center on “Cosmic Interacting Matter” and are therefore especially interested in plasma‑physics applications in astrophysical environments as well as in magnetic‑confinement fusion. Recently, we have also turned to the Wetterich equation, an exact equation of the functional renormalization group, providing a systematic framework to study many‑body and field‑theoretic models such as classical and quantum phase transitions in solid‑state physics.

As a research assistant (m/f/x), you will independently develop new numerical schemes, implement and test their properties as well as analyze their numerical properties in challenging application problems. The opportunity to pursue further academic qualifications (a Ph.D.) is offered and encouraged.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 36
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-10-13

Your tasks:

- Research in scientific computing with the focus on the development and efficient implementation of numerical methods for hyperbolic differential equation
- Implementation of efficient algorithms for application problems
- Writing of papers for publication in highly ranked international journals
- Teaching in applied mathematics

Your profile:

jobs.description:
The Leibniz-Institut für Analytische Wissenschaften - ISAS - e. V. develops efficient analytical methods for health research. Thus, it contributes to the improvement of the prevention, early diagnosis, and therapy of diseases like cardiovascular diseases or cancer. Overall, the institute strives to advance precision medicine by combining knowledge from different fields such as biology, chemistry, computer science, medicine, pharmacology, and physics. ISAS is a member of the Leibniz Association and is publicly funded by the Federal Republic of Germany and its federal states.

In the department Bioanalytics for the Multidimensional OMICS Data Analysis research group, we invite applications for a:

PhD Candidate (m/f/d)

This position is part of the Leibniz Science Campus “Cardio-Oncology Campus for Precision Medicine”, with focus on the analysis and development of biomarker profiles for the personalized assessment of cardiovascular risks associated with cancer therapy.

Non-residents who apply for this job will receive help from the institute to find accommodation and to handle authorities. Applications from disabled applicants are welcome. ISAS supports the principle of equal opportunity for all employees and therefore particularly encourages women to apply.

The full-time position is available immediately. It is fixed-termed and offered until September 30, 2030. The salary will be according to the German TV-L and falls within the pay group 13. The time limitation of the contract is based on the Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz (WissZeitVG).
Analysis of phenotypic, microscopic, PET/MRI, MALDI-MSI, and LC-MS/MS data
Development of AI-based models for personalized risk assessment
Validation and application of model performance using established biomarkers and patient cohorts
Evaluation, analysis, and visualization of data
Documentation of laboratory work
Collaboration with project partners and regular presentation of results

M.Sc. or Diploma in bioinformatics or a comparable qualification
Extensive programming experience
Practical experience in machine learning and the application of large language models
Knowledge of OMICS and image data analysis
A willingness to engage in interdisciplinary scientific work, the ability to work in a team, an open-minded attitude, and a commitment to the work are required
Strong communication skills, organisational talent and a solution-oriented approach
Proficiency in MS Office
Willingness to travel for work
Excellent written and spoken English; German would be an advantage

A clear research topic as well as multifold training and support for PhD students in framework of ISAS and the Leibniz association
Training and scientific development opportunities in an international environment and an excellent working atmosphere in a very dynamic and professional team
Extensive state-of-the-art equipment and infrastructure in various analytical methods
The opportunity to present your data on international conferences and participate in workshops
A wide range of opportunities for further training and qualifications
Flexible working times, mobile working and attractive social benefits
Family-friendly facilities and support from a family service

jobs.occupation: IMPACT PORTFOLIO MANAGER (Fairer Futures Programmes) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description:
Overview:

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Role purpose: 

The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. 

The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.

Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.

Main Responsibilities:            

- MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.
- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Work with PNs to ensure that MEL frameworks for individual projects within both programme portfolios are aligned to the overarching programme frameworks, providing where capacity is available guidance and quality assurance at project inception and during implementation
- Reporting, Synthesis, and Learning. Lead the preparation of programme-level MEL reporting for programmes, synthesising data and evidence from across the programme portfolio into outputs that feed into the overall strategy reporting cycle. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.
- Programme Evaluation. Lead the design, commissioning, and management of the programme evaluations. This includes developing evaluation questions in collaboration with PNs and Global Product Teams, overseeing evaluation partners, and ensuring findings are translated into actionable learning.
- Impact Services and External Engagement. Identify opportunities to offer MEL technical services to Fairtrade system organisations and external partners, drawing on expertise developed through the programmes. Contribute to the scoping, design, and pitching of impact services in collaboration with the Head, with a particular focus on programme MEL, data collection design, and evaluation. Participate actively in relevant system-wide working groups, representing the Impact Management team's MEL perspective on cross-organisational initiatives.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree or higher in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years' experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, with demonstrable experience designing and managing MEL frameworks for multi-stakeholder projects or programmes. At least two years' experience working in or with stakeholders from the Global South, preferably in agricultural or commodity supply chain contexts. Experience in coffee and bananas is an advantage.

Language requirements: Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is a advantage. 

Job Specific Competencies/knowledge: 

- Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning
- Project and Programme Management
- International Development Expertise
- Stakeholder Management
- Planning and execution
- Data Collection Design and Management
- Evaluation Design and Commissioning
- Enhancing data-driven decision making
- Data Analysis (quantitative and qualitative)
- Data Reporting and Synthesis
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Customer Service
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Feedback sourcing

Software/Tools: 

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner)
- Kobo Toolbox (or similar survey design and implementation tools)
- Miro (or similar online whiteboarding tools)
- Canva (or similar graphic design tools)
- Claude.ai (or similar AI  tools)
- Toladata (or similar project monitoring MEL platform)
- Power BI (or similar business intelligence software)

TERMS AND CONDITIONS:

- This is a two-year full-time position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English.
- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments starting from €5455 Gross per month
- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  
- 30 days of holidays per year (for fulltime employees)
- Subsidised public transportation ticket
- Subsidised meal services
- Childcare cost subsidy 

Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.
